subject: Computer Networking
title: UWB: Precision Location
description: A fast breakdown of UWB: Precision Location for builders.

hook.text: Your phone tells you your keys are exactly 2.3 meters away, behind the couch. UWB makes that precision possible.

buildup.text: Ultra-Wideband sends very short pulses across a wide frequency range. The timing of pulses reveals precise distance.

discovery.text: UWB achieves centimeter-level accuracy. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi can only estimate within a few meters.

twist.text: UWB is also secure against relay attacks. Car keys using UWB know if you're actually next to the car.

climax.text: Apple AirTags, Samsung SmartTags, and new car key systems all use UWB for precise spatial awareness.

punchline.text: UWB knows where things are. Not roughly — precisely.

quiz.question: What makes UWB more precise than Bluetooth for location?
options: It measures time-of-flight of very short pulses with centimeter accuracy
It uses a stronger radio signal
It connects to GPS satellites directly

details.summary: Ultra-Wideband uses very short radio pulses across a wide frequency range to determine device positions with centimeter-level accuracy. UWB powers AirTags, car digital keys, and precise indoor navigation.
details.whyItMatters: UWB brings centimeter-level positioning indoors where GPS cannot reach. This precision enables new interactions like directional finding, secure access control, and spatial awareness for devices.
takeaways: UWB achieves centimeter-level positioning using time-of-flight
Apple AirTag and Samsung SmartTag use UWB for precise finding
Time-of-flight ranging resists relay attacks on digital car keys

faq.question: How does UWB achieve centimeter accuracy?
faq.answer: UWB sends billions of very short pulses per second across a wide frequency band. The receiver measures the exact time each pulse takes to arrive. Since radio waves travel at the speed of light, tiny time differences correspond to centimeter-level distance measurements.

faq.question: How is UWB more secure than Bluetooth for location?
faq.answer: Bluetooth measures signal strength to estimate distance, which attackers can amplify to spoof proximity. UWB measures time-of-flight, which cannot be shortened — the speed of light is constant.
